title: Stop a worker when pi goes silent, not when a wall clock fires
description:
CORRECTED 2026-09-22. The first version of this tick said pi workers hung on a dropped connection. That was WRONG, and it led to three working attempts being killed by hand.

WHAT ACTUALLY HAPPENED, from pi's own session logs (~/.pi/agent/sessions/<worktree>/…jsonl), which record every turn:

  attempt  span               tool calls  writes  max gap between entries
  w9b#3    15:57 -> 16:36     97          0       562s
  keh#3    16:09 -> 16:37     75          6       126s
  w9b#4    16:42 -> 16:59     41          0       163s
  keh#4    16:42 -> 17:10+    51          6       223s

Every one was working until the moment it was killed. keh#3 wrote its first file at 16:29, about four minutes AFTER the run warned it had 'written NOTHING into its worktree' for 15 minutes. GLM 5.3 spends a long orientation phase reading before it writes, and on a hard tick that phase is 15-40 minutes.

WHY THE DIAGNOSIS WENT WRONG, recorded so nobody repeats it: pi's own process CPU and socket count do not measure its work. The thinking happens on the model; the tool calls run as short-lived child processes whose CPU is not pi's. 'Alive, ~0% CPU, one open socket to Cloudflare, no worktree changes' is what a pi worker looks like while it waits for GLM's next turn. It is indistinguishable from a hang by those signals.

THE ACTUAL DEFECT: the liveness observable. The stall warning measures bytes in the worktree and branch movement, which are silent through a whole orientation phase. pi appends to its session log on EVERY turn, so the log's growth is a precise, cheap liveness signal that exists already and costs nothing to read. A worker whose session log has not grown in N minutes is stalled; one whose worktree has not changed is merely reading.

And the corollary for gvc and the unattended factory: an automatic interrupt built on the worktree signal would have killed these same three working attempts. Nothing may act on liveness until the observable is right.

Nothing was lost in the kills: keh#3's six files were snapshotted to refs/ticfac/wip/run-epic-xte/tick-keh/attempt-3 and handed to keh#4 as a prior snapshot.
notes:
2026-09-22 19:34 - OPERATOR, 2026-09-22, and this widens the tick from a warning to the stop itself:

  'actually a worker should not be interrupted after 3600s, many ticks can take longer'
  'Pi's last output is a really good gauge of stall-ness'

So the fixed wall clock stops being the primary bound. The two statements are one mechanism: the
thing that should stop a worker is SILENCE, measured on the runner's own turn log, not elapsed time.

Measured today, as the starting point for the silence default (max gap between consecutive session
entries in attempts that were all working): 126s, 163s, 166s, 224s, 562s. The 562s gap was a single
long GLM turn in w9b try 1 and the worker carried on normally after it. So a silence bound under ~10
minutes would have killed a healthy worker; 15-20 minutes clears every gap seen so far with margin.

Where the timer lives today: internal/exec/subprocess/supervisor.go:236-260 sets a time.NewTimer
from record.WallSeconds once at supervisor start, so a live attempt's bound cannot be changed. The
silence check belongs beside it in the supervisor: it already holds the runner pid and the worktree,
and the session log path follows from the worktree path.

record.go:543 refuses wall_seconds <= 0 because 'an unbounded job is one nothing stops'. That
principle survives this change intact: the silence bound IS what stops it. Keep a large absolute
backstop if one is wanted at all, and say in the code that it is the backstop, not the bound.

Tooling that already reads this log: ~/.local/bin/pi-follow (written 2026-09-22) parses the same
jsonl and shows every tool call and write live.
2026-09-22 19:39 - Found while restarting both runs with -wall 86400 (2026-09-22 17:38): the stall warning on an ADOPTED attempt names the new run's -wall, not the bound the attempt actually carries. w9b dispatch #5 was issued with wall_seconds=3600 and its supervisor's timer is fixed at that; after the restart the warning read 'the wall clock of 86400s is still the bound', which is false - it is stopped at 18:03. The message should read the attempt record's wall_seconds. Moot once the silence bound replaces the wall clock, but until then it tells an operator the wrong deadline.
acceptance_criteria: A worker is stopped when its runner's own turn log (pi's session jsonl) has not grown for a bounded silence period, not when a fixed wall clock fires; a worker taking turns is never stopped for elapsed time alone, so a tick may legitimately run longer than an hour; the silence bound is configurable with a default justified from measured turn gaps; any remaining absolute wall clock is a large backstop, documented as such, not the primary bound; the stall warning reports silence duration rather than worktree idleness; a test drives a worker that is slow-but-talking (never stopped) and one that goes silent (stopped); and the 'an unbounded job is one nothing stops' refusal in record.go still holds, because the silence bound is the thing that stops it
